sources.title: An extreme mutational hotspot in nlpD depends on transcriptional induction of rpoS
sources.inspection: Full primary article XML; Results, Methods, Discussion, data/code statements and embedded captions inspected; supplements/source data not acquired.
sources.domain: Pseudomonas fluorescens SBW25; selected cell-chaining evolution in Δwss, with reporter mutation assays in SBW25 and ΔpsrA.
tmd_implications_original_analysis: Exact sequence context, promoter induction and growth phase can alter site-specific supply; a genome-wide average cannot substitute for a route-specific baseline.
Promoter/PsrA genetic contrasts support transcription dependence in this reporter system, while the precise chemical lesion mechanism and transport to native nlpD remain unresolved.
limits: Selected CC populations suppress WS competition via Δwss, so their counts are not common-background W/A/M route shares.
Mutation estimates use a distal selectable rpoSp-kan reporter, not unaltered native nlpD; the article explicitly identifies native-site transport uncertainty.

Fluctuation estimates depend on growth and neutrality assumptions; supporting captions report a small significant reporter fitness reduction. No source-data ZIP or supplementary DOCX/PDF bytes were acquired.

sources.title: Mutation-biased adaptation is consequential even in large bacterial populations
sources.inspection: Full primary article XML; Results, Methods, Discussion, data/code statements and embedded captions inspected; supplements/source data not acquired.
sources.domain: E. coli AB1157 ampC-deleted ΔmutH/ΔmutT backgrounds carrying plasmid blaTEM-1; serial cefotaxime escalation across five culture-volume regimes.
tmd_implications_original_analysis: Population size, mutation spectrum, step length and selection alignment can jointly change adaptive endpoints; large populations do not alone remove mutation-supply effects.
Preserve extinction/no-success outcomes and distinguish multi-mutation endpoint genotypes from mutually exclusive first-arrival routes; culture volume may also change biological conditions.
limits: Two different repair-mutator backgrounds and TEM-1/PBP3-associated endpoints are not a common-ancestor W/A/M panel.
Endpoint Sanger isolates were chosen among longest-surviving lineages; a genotype may carry mutations in both targets. These observations are not single-route first winners.

Simulation outcomes rely on specified additive fitness and pathway lengths; empirical effective population sizes were adjusted downward when comparing curves, so agreement is not a locked held-out prediction.
Raw source data, supplementary files, SRA reads and simulation repository code were not acquired or executed.

sources.title: Tuning evolvability via plasmid copy number and regulatory architecture
sources.inspection: Full primary article XML; Results, Methods, Discussion, data/code statements and embedded captions inspected; supplements/source data not acquired.
sources.domain: Engineered E. coli DH5α and DH5αΔlacI::ampR with EvolvR mutagenesis, pSC101 copy-number variants and fluorescence/resistance circuits.
tmd_implications_original_analysis: Observed phenotypic mutation frequency depends on the genotype-to-phenotype mapping and detection threshold; generated DNA changes and detectable mutant events are different quantities.
Copy-number-dependent complementation/masking provides established genetic-dominance and regulation alternatives; it does not identify a new TMD natural-dominance force.
limits: Engineered plasmid multiploidy and targeted EvolvR mutagenesis differ from chromosomal W/A/M evolution; no numerical parameter is transferred.
Flow-cytometry events are cell measurements, not independent founding-culture or known-introduced fixed-route recovery trials.
The flow protocol divides a diluted overnight culture into eight wells; biological founder independence is not inferred from plotted eight replicates. Regrowth and gates affect the observed outcome.
Source-data files, supplementary figures, sequencing accessions and archived code were not acquired or executed.
